text.p: The Australia and New Zealand Banking Group Ltd (ANZ) reported a better than expected six percent rise in net profit for the 1995/96 year on Wednesday.

But the A$1.116 billion net profit for the year to September 30, above analysts' expectations of about A$1.05 billion, was due largely to strong performance from ANZ's overseas units and disguised a sharp rise in operating costs and a lower profit from ANZ's Australian operations.
ANZ managing director Don Mercer said however after the release of the results that these costs would fall and that profits would continue to rise in the current 1996/97 year.
Asked by reporters if he expected growth in the bottom line in 1996/97, chief executive Don Mercer said: "That's certainly what a lot of people are expecting. We expect it of ourselves."
Mercer also predicted costs would decline in the later part of fiscal 1996/97.
"Our costs are going to be flat in the first half of next year and they will be coming down in the second half," he said.
Mercer said higher personnel costs were the main factor in the rise in operating expenses to A$3.64 billion in 1995/96 from A$3.33 billion the previous year.
